analysis:
Both changed files are test-only Swift check executables (provider-swift/Tests/ClusterOnboardingChecks/OnboardingChecks.swift and provider-swift/Tests/ClusterSupervisionChecks/main.swift). No production source, auth, attestation, encryption, or coordinator wire code changed in the supplied units. The OnboardingChecks hunk (head lines 1257-1262) adds assertions for ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild: re-plan only when both Macs report the same new build, and wait on a nil, missing, or old-build answer. The remainder of the first unit and the second unit are unchanged context. It includes the local-only scope bind validation tests (isValidBind rejecting 'my-mac.local' and '0.0.0.0;x') and checks that no credential, host, address, or SSH text appears in transcripts. Those are pre-existing and relevant to TB-013 and A-019 only loosely.

The ClusterSupervisionChecks hunk (head 248-330) adds assertions for the new ClusterPairUpdate coordination: the shared slot keyed on cluster ID, wait/ready/gaveUp states, and a stale-progress and silent-partner fallback to cannotCoordinate. It also covers phase-forward-compat decoding (an unknown phase decodes as .checking and is waited for, never read as ready), and a request file taken once, dropped when older than an hour, and removed. The tests encode sound fail-safe behaviour: ordering that stops both Macs from installing different releases, and no install before both are drained.

The production implementations (ClusterPairUpdate, ClusterPairUpdateProgress, the request and progress file handling in service-update-request.json and service-update.json) are not in the supplied evidence. Their file permissions, ownership checks, and whether a same-UID local process could forge progress or request files to stall or steer updates (cf. T-059/T-060, T-043) cannot be assessed here. The partner progress transport between Macs is also unverified. Those are questions for the pass that sees the non-test sources. No finding is raised against the tests themselves.
